cards.hint: Recall how high the column grows in a short time.
options: more than 12 miles above a volcano
cards.quote: Eruption columns can grow rapidly and reach more than 12 miles above a volcano in less than 30 minutes, forming an eruption cloud.
cards.stem: How far above a volcano can a rapid eruption column reach?

cards.hint: Compare this to slower lava and lahar speeds.
cards.quote: These pyroclastic flows can be as hot as 1,500°F and move at speeds of 100 to 150 miles per hour.
cards.stem: At what speeds can pyroclastic flows move down a volcano?

cards.hint: Think of wet concrete moving down river valleys.
cards.quote: These flows of mud, rock, and water can rush down valleys and stream channels at speeds of 20 to 40 miles per hour and can travel more than 50 miles.
cards.stem: How fast can lahars rush down valleys and stream channels?

cards.hint: Think of ash covering several states in the west.
cards.quote: Ash from the May 18, 1980, eruption of Mount St. Helens, Washington, fell over an area of 22,000 square miles in the Western United States.
cards.stem: How large an area was covered by ash from the 1980 Mount St. Helens eruption?
